question.text: Meena holds 200 shares of DEF Ltd. (FV Rs.2 each). If the company announces a stock consolidation from FV Rs.2 to FV Rs.10, how many shares will Meena hold after consolidation?

explanation.text: The Logic: Increasing face value from Rs.2 to Rs.10 means 5 old shares are consolidated into 1 new share. Total face value held = 200 x Rs.2 = Rs.400; post-consolidation = Rs.400 / Rs.10 = 40 shares. The value held remains unchanged. The Trap: Candidates may multiply instead of divide (getting 1,000 shares), confusing consolidation with a split. In consolidation, face value increases and the share count decreases. Note: In a consolidation the number of shares falls in inverse proportion to the increase in face value; the aggregate face value remains the same.
